clean_source_blocks.text: A 67-million-year-old Tyrannosaurus rex nicknamed Gus is expected to become one of the most expensive dinosaur fossils ever sold when it goes up for auction at Sotheby's in New York on Tuesday. Valued at up to $30 million, the skeleton could sell for even more if bidding intensifies, potentially setting another milestone in the booming fossil market. The auction has reignited a long-running debate in the scientific community. While auctioneers and fossil hunters argue that years of difficult excavation deserve financial reward, many paleontologists fear Gus could disappear into a private collection, limiting future research on one of the most complete T. rex specimens ever discovered. The sale reflects a growing trend in which dinosaur fossils are increasingly viewed as high-value collectibles, leaving museums struggling to compete with wealthy private buyers.
The dinosaur skeleton, which roamed the planet 67 million years ago, was sold by Sotheby's in New York.

The nearly complete South Dakota specimen set a new record for a dino at auction. by Jo Lawson-Tancred Jul 14, 2026 ShareShare This Article One of the largest, most complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeletons ever found set a new record for a dinosaur at auction when it fetched $50 million at Sotheby’s natural history auction in New York today, after a tense 10 minutes of bidding. The previous record holder was the Stegosaurus, dubbed Apex, which sold for $44 million to hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin at Sotheby’s in 2024. The mighty T.Rex soared past presale expectations of $20 million–$30 million—the highest estimate ever fixed to a fossil—eventually hammering at $43 million. The final price of just over $50 million includes buyer’s fees. “Try a bigger bite,” auctioneer Phyllis Kao goaded during a brief bidding lull. “It’s a T.Rex after all!”

Preserved for around 67 million years in the Hell Creek Formation of South Dakota, the dino, known as Gus, was excavated between 2021 and 2023. With about 61 percent of his skeleton recovered, Gus is an unusually complete specimen and was painstakingly reconstructed in a “predatory pose” mount, with his head turned and one foot slightly raised. Standing 12 feet high and measuring 38 feet long, he was a fearsome sight to behold in the Breuer building. Gus the Tyrannosaurus rex. Photo: Matthew Sherman, courtesy of Sotheby’s.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World | URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c0qyq800n44o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss]
A 67 million-year-old Tyrannosaurus rex has been sold for £37.4m ($50.1m) at a Sotheby's auction in New York - the most ever paid for a dinosaur.

The fossil of this infamous predator stands more than 12 feet (4m) tall, and with over 60% of its bones recovered is one of "the most complete" specimens ever found, according to Sotheby's.

The winning bidder at the sale on Tuesday has not yet been disclosed.

Gus, as the T. rex has been affectionately named, was discovered in 2021 on a remote ranch in the US State of South Dakota.

New dinosaur species as long as cricket pitch discovered in Thailand

"It's really incredible to see and to have the level of public interest," said Cassandra Hatton, Sotheby's worldwide head of science and natural history.

"I think anytime you've got this, it is good for science. In general, more people are going to go to the museums, it adds dinosaurs and natural history into the conversation."

The sale exceeded the previous record set by a stegosaurus in 2024, and is the first to exceed the $50m benchmark.

Some scientists have told the BBC that the auction may herald a new era in fossil collecting by the ultra-rich.

The skull indicated a life of danger for the T. rex nicknamed Gus

Hatton says the price paid reflects the time and resources that went into uncovering the specimen.

The bones were excavated over three summers, when it was warm enough for the ground to have thawed, from 2021 to 2023.

But it took a further three years in the lab to piece the T. rex back together.

This work revealed the skull had bite marks, and previously broken ribs that had healed in its lifetime.

Both injuries were potentially sustained during scavenging or during a battle with other dinosaurs.

It may be some time before the buyer is revealed, but Apex, the stegosaurus who held the last record, was loaned out to the American Natural History Museum for four years by its billionaire-owner Kenneth Griffin.

So, even if Gus has attracted an ultra-wealthy buyer it still might be coming to a museum near you soon.

payload.title: T. rex -luuranko Gus myytiin ennätyksellisellä 50 miljoonalla dollarilla
payload.summary: Etelä-Dakotasta löydetty Gus teki New Yorkissa uuden dinosaurusten huutokauppaennätyksen. Noin 67 miljoonaa vuotta vanhasta luurangosta on säilynyt 61 prosenttia.
payload.content:
Yksi suurimmista ja täydellisimmistä koskaan löydetyistä Tyrannosaurus rex -luurangoista on myyty New Yorkissa hieman yli 50 miljoonalla dollarilla. Gus-niminen, noin 67 miljoonaa vuotta vanha fossiili teki Sotheby'sin luonnonhistoriallisessa huutokaupassa uuden dinosaurusten huutokauppaennätyksen ja ylitti selvästi sille asetetun 20–30 miljoonan dollarin ennakkoarvion.

## Kymmenen minuutin tarjouskilpailu

Tiistain tarjouskilpailu kesti noin kymmenen minuuttia. Luurangon vasarahinnaksi nousi 43 miljoonaa dollaria, ja ostajalta perittävät maksut nostivat lopullisen hinnan hieman yli 50 miljoonaan dollariin. Vasarahinta ylitti ennakkoarvion ylärajan 13 miljoonalla dollarilla. Meklari Phyllis Kao kannusti tarjoajia jatkamaan, kun tarjouskilpailu hetkeksi hiljeni.

Aiempi huutokauppaennätys kuului Apex-nimiselle Stegosaurus-luurangolle, joka myytiin Sotheby'sillä vuonna 2024 44 miljoonalla dollarilla miljardööri Ken Griffinille. Gusin ennakkoarvio oli jo itsessään korkein fossiilille koskaan asetettu arvio.

## Luurangosta on säilynyt 61 prosenttia

Gus löytyi Etelä-Dakotan Hell Creek -muodostumasta, jossa sen jäänteet olivat säilyneet noin 67 miljoonaa vuotta. Fossiilia kaivettiin esiin vuosina 2021–2023. Luurangosta on saatu talteen noin 61 prosenttia, minkä vuoksi sitä pidetään poikkeuksellisen täydellisenä T. rex -yksilönä.

Näyttelyä varten luuranko koottiin saalistavaa asentoa muistuttavaan muotoon: pää on kääntynyt sivulle ja toinen jalka hieman koholla. Gus on noin 3,7 metriä korkea ja 11,6 metriä pitkä.

## Ennätyshinnat huolestuttavat tutkijoita

Ennätyskauppa nostaa jälleen esiin paleontologien pitkään esittämän huolen harvinaisten fossiilien päätymisestä yksityiskokoelmiin. Tutkijat pelkäävät, että tällöin tieteellisesti arvokkaiden näytteiden saatavuus tutkimukseen voi rajoittua. Gusin kaltaisen, verrattain täydellisen T. rex -luurangon kohdalla kysymys on erityisen merkittävä.

Kiistan ytimessä on se, säilyvätkö merkittävät löydöt tutkijoiden ulottuvilla vai muuttuvatko ne ensisijaisesti kalliiksi keräilykohteiksi. Huutokauppatalot ja fossiilien etsijät puolestaan korostavat, että vaikeat ja vuosia kestävät kaivaukset ansaitsevat taloudellisen korvauksen. Fossiilien hintojen nousu tekee niistä yhä halutumpia keräilykohteita, mutta samalla museoiden on vaikea kilpailla varakkaiden yksityisostajien kanssa.

Huutokauppatalot ja fossiilien etsijät puolestaan korostavat, että vaikeat ja vuosia kestävät kaivaukset ansaitsevat taloudellisen korvauksen. Fossiilien hintojen nousu tekee niistä yhä halutumpia keräilykohteita, mutta samalla museoiden on vaikea kilpailla varakkaiden yksityisostajien kanssa.

article.source_text:
A 67-million-year-old Tyrannosaurus rex nicknamed Gus is expected to become one of the most expensive dinosaur fossils ever sold when it goes up for auction at Sotheby's in New York on Tuesday. Valued at up to $30 million, the skeleton could sell for even more if bidding intensifies, potentially setting another milestone in the booming fossil market. The auction has reignited a long-running debate in the scientific community. While auctioneers and fossil hunters argue that years of difficult excavation deserve financial reward, many paleontologists fear Gus could disappear into a private collection, limiting future research on one of the most complete T. rex specimens ever discovered. The sale reflects a growing trend in which dinosaur fossils are increasingly viewed as high-value collectibles, leaving museums struggling to compete with wealthy private buyers.

The dinosaur skeleton, which roamed the planet 67 million years ago, was sold by Sotheby's in New York.

The nearly complete South Dakota specimen set a new record for a dino at auction. by Jo Lawson-Tancred Jul 14, 2026 ShareShare This Article One of the largest, most complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeletons ever found set a new record for a dinosaur at auction when it fetched $50 million at Sotheby’s natural history auction in New York today, after a tense 10 minutes of bidding. The previous record holder was the Stegosaurus, dubbed Apex, which sold for $44 million to hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin at Sotheby’s in 2024. The mighty T.Rex soared past presale expectations of $20 million–$30 million—the highest estimate ever fixed to a fossil—eventually hammering at $43 million. The final price of just over $50 million includes buyer’s fees. “Try a bigger bite,” auctioneer Phyllis Kao goaded during a brief bidding lull. “It’s a T.Rex after all!”

Preserved for around 67 million years in the Hell Creek Formation of South Dakota, the dino, known as Gus, was excavated between 2021 and 2023. With about 61 percent of his skeleton recovered, Gus is an unusually complete specimen and was painstakingly reconstructed in a “predatory pose” mount, with his head turned and one foot slightly raised. Standing 12 feet high and measuring 38 feet long, he was a fearsome sight to behold in the Breuer building. Gus the Tyrannosaurus rex. Photo: Matthew Sherman, courtesy of Sotheby’s.
